title: CONFIRMED: 'Require MFA for all users' (mfa_required_for_all) is never enforced server-side — a password-only login mints a full 24h superuser JWT and the enforcement signal is an advisory response flag the SPA alone acts on
evidence: All cited lines were opened and match verbatim, so the citation stands unchanged. auth.go:133 `needBind := sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled` sits AFTER `token, err := auth.Issue(s.secret, u.ID, u.Username)` (auth.go:125) and is returned as plain data: `134: s.ok(c, gin.H{` / `135: "token": token,` / `137: "need_bind_mfa": needBind,` / `138: })`. auth/jwt.go:11-15 `type Claims struct { UserID uint; Username string; jwt.RegisteredClaims }` — no amr/mfa claim exists to gate on, expiry 24h (jwt.go:21). backend/internal/admin/middleware.go read end-to-end (33 lines): AuthMiddleware does only `if !strings.HasPrefix(h, "Bearer ")` (17), `claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, token)` (23), `c.Set("operator"...)`/`c.Set("userID"...)` (29-30) — no AdminUser load, no MFA state. grep `MFAEnabled|mfa_enabled|MFABoundAt` in backend/ → only auth.go (86, 133, 136, 148, 195, 206, 244, 263, 279), users.go (13, 27, 44, 49-50), model.go (18-19), settings.go (80, 87); grep `MFARequiredAll|mfa_required_for_all|GraceDays|grace_days` in backend/ → exactly 4 hits (auth.go:133, settings.go:81, settings.go:83, settings.go:87), i.e. GraceDays is declared+defaulted (7) and never read, while Security.tsx:113-115 exposes a required `grace_days` field labelled 'Enforcement Grace Period'. grep `gin.HandlerFunc` in the admin package returns ONE result (middleware.go:14) and routes.go:43-148 gates every protected route with `s.AuthMiddleware()` alone — no second middleware, no role check. Frontend claims verified: Login.tsx:45 `setAuth(res.token, res.user)` executes before `46: if (res.need_bind_mfa) { 47: message.warning(...) 48: navigate('/account/security', { replace: true })` — the redirect happens inside an already-authenticated session; store/auth.ts:33 `export const isLoggedIn = () => Boolean(useAuthStore.getState().token)`; App.tsx:67-72 RequireAuth checks only isLoggedIn(); AccountSecurity.tsx:314-318 is the `{me && !bound && step === 0 && (...)} t('acctSec.forcedTip')` hint paragraph. Labels: i18n/locales/zh-CN/pages/security.ts:8 `'security.mfaRequired': '强制所有用户启用 MFA'`, en-US/pages/security.ts:8 'Require MFA for All Users' vs :9 `'...users without MFA are guided through enrollment after login'`.
impact: The differential is the whole point of the toggle: a user who HAS bound MFA and presents only a password gets `{mfa_required:true, mfa_token}` (auth.go:87-91) and never a token; a user who has NOT bound MFA and presents the same single factor gets a fully privileged JWT (auth.go:110 → 125). Skipping enrolment is free server-side — the only consequence is a client-side redirect an attacker never executes, so `curl` against /api/admin/v1/* works. Two corroborating facts (new to the original report) make this worse than hygiene: (a) There is NO user-creation endpoint (routes.go:133-135 is only GET /users, POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa, POST /users/:id/unlock); the single admin account comes from cmd/server/main.go:179 `u := model.AdminUser{Username: cfg.AdminUser, PasswordHash: string(hash)}`, which leaves MFAEnabled at Go's zero value false. So in the default one-admin deployment, enabling 'Require MFA for All Users' changes nothing at all — the console displays a policy that the only existing account structurally cannot satisfy, while still authenticating it with one factor. (b) That one-factor token is a total-compromise token, because the security policy itself is writable without any second factor: PUT /settings/security → admin/settings.go:115-128 `saveSecurity` persists attacker JSON with zero validation and login re-reads it per request (auth.go:43 `sec := s.securitySettings()` → server.go:52-56 LoadKV), so `mfa_enabled:false` retroactively makes every already-bound admin single-factor on their next login (auth.go:86 short-circuits); and POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa → admin/users.go:37-52 force-clears another user's `mfa_secret`/`mfa_enabled`/`recovery_codes_json` with no TOTP, no password re-entry, only an audit row (users.go:50). Add GET /config/export + /backups/:id/download and API-key/provider CRUD, and a phished or default (`admin123`, main.go:172) password bypasses the organisation's declared compensating control and then destroys it for everyone else.
mitigations_checked: Verified present, and none of them closes the gap for unbound users: 2FA is enforced for users who have bound it (auth.go:86-108); the mfa_token branch cannot be walked through without a second factor (`66: if !ok2 { s.onMFAFail(&u); s.fail(c, 40103, ...) }`, tickets single-use `47: s.mfa().PopLoginTicket` and uid-bound `52: if uid != u.ID`); self-service bind requires a valid TOTP (auth.go:236) and self-service unbind a valid TOTP or consumed recovery code (auth.go:268-277, consumeRecoveryCode hashes compared at mfa.go:63-75); recovery codes stored SHA-256-hashed (mfa.go:50); mfaSetup refuses over an existing binding (auth.go:206-209); password/MFA failure lockout 5→15min (auth.go:114-122). NOT mitigations: no login rate limiting (the quota.RateLimiter/RedisLimiter is wired only into the gateway — main.go:63-67, gateway.go:40); docs/api-contract.md:44 documents the token+need_bind_mfa shape, so this is a security-design/labelling defect rather than code violating its own spec, and the en-US tooltip honestly says 'guided' — but neither adds any server-side check. JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY defaults and HS256 pinning are pre-agreed architecture facts, not re-reported here.
recommendation: Enforce in the authenticated group, not in the SPA: add a middleware (or extend AuthMiddleware) that loads the AdminUser and returns a dedicated 403/40302 when `sec.MFAEnabled && sec.MFARequiredAll && !u.MFAEnabled`, allow-listing only /auth/me, /auth/password and /account/mfa/*; or refuse to issue a privileged token at login until binding completes (issue a scoped enrolment-only token / add an `amr` claim and honour it in the gate). Independently, require second-factor proof for the security-self-destruct endpoints (`PUT /settings/security`, `POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa`) and never accept them from a session that satisfied only one factor. Either implement `grace_days` against `u.MFABoundAt`/`CreatedAt` with a hard block on expiry, or delete the field and its required form input. Rename the control away from 'require/强制' while it is advisory, and note that with no user-creation endpoint the bootstrap admin (main.go:179) is the account that must be forced to enrol.
reason: Confirmed as filed, severity high upheld, no line correction. Every quoted location was read end-to-end and matched verbatim: auth.go:133-138 (token issued at :125, before needBind is even computed; flag is response data only), middleware.go:14-31 (signature-only validation, no user/MFA lookup), settings.go:87 (MFARequiredAll default false, GraceDays 7), auth/jwt.go:11-27 (no claim available to gate on), routes.go:43-148 + grep `gin.HandlerFunc` (AuthMiddleware is the single gate for the entire admin API), Login.tsx:45-48 (setAuth before the advisory navigate), store/auth.ts:33 + App.tsx:67-72 (auth guard = token presence only), AccountSecurity.tsx:314-318 (hint paragraph), i18n security.ts:8-9 (label '强制所有用户启用 MFA'/'Require MFA for All Users' vs tooltip 'guided through enrollment'). The two greps the finding leans on reproduce exactly: MFARequiredAll has one functional reference (auth.go:133) and GraceDays has zero. Chain integrity: the control withheld by this defect is the second factor itself, and the code demonstrably withholds it from bound users (auth.go:87-91) while granting a full token to unbound ones — so the attacker does NOT already hold the privilege the control protects. I checked the standard refutation angles and none hold: no server-side grace/enforcement state exists, the input (login credentials) is attacker-reachable over the network with no rate limiting on POST /auth/login, and the only 'enforcement' is client-side navigation that any non-browser client skips. I also reinforced the finding with two facts it did not state: (1) the bootstrap admin is created with MFAEnabled unset and there is no user-creation route, so in a default single-admin deployment the toggle is non-functional by construction; (2) a single-factor token can immediately set mfa_enabled=false via the unvalidated saveSecurity, or force-unbind a bound user via users.go:37-52 without any TOTP — turning a password leak into durable removal of 2FA for the legitimate operator, on top of full config/backup/API-key access. Downgrade to medium was considered because exploitation requires first-factor credentials, because MFARequiredAll defaults to false, and because the tooltip + api-contract disclose the advisory behaviour; rejected — the defect is precisely that a control an operator can legitimately turn on (and that ships with an 'Enforcement Grace Period' knob implying server-side enforcement) has no server-side effect at all, and the resulting token reaches account takeover, MFA policy destruction and data exfiltration paths. High = authed-but-severe / account takeover, matching the rubric; not critical, since it is not reachable unauthenticated.
exploit_sketch:
Precondition: an admin account with mfa_enabled=false — the state of the ONLY account in a default deployment (main.go:179 leaves MFAEnabled zero; no user-creation route exists). Operator has PUT /api/admin/v1/settings/security {"mfa_enabled":true,"mfa_required_for_all":true,"recovery_code_count":10,"grace_days":7}, believing all admin logins are two-factor.

1) Get the password (default `admin123` per main.go:172, phish, reuse) — no browser/SPA required:
   TOK=$(curl -sS -X POST http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r .data.token)
   Response is code:0 with data.token AND data.need_bind_mfa:true (auth.go:133-138); auth.go:86 is skipped because u.MFAEnabled==false, so no mfa_required step is ever presented. $TOK is a valid HS256 admin JWT for 24h.
2) Use it anywhere — AuthMiddleware only verifies the signature:
   curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/users
   curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/config/export
3) Destroy the control for all other admins (no re-auth, and login re-reads the KV via auth.go:43):
   curl -sS -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"mfa_enabled":false,"mfa_required_for_all":false,"recovery_code_count":10,"grace_days":0}' http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/settings/security
   — or strip one victim's device with no TOTP: curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" http://target:8080/api/admin/v1/users/1/unbind-mfa (users.go:48-49)
Only cost of skipping enrolment: the SPA's navigate('/account/security') at Login.tsx:48. `grace_days` is never read anywhere in backend/, so there is no enforcement window to wait out.
